steps.name: Team-preview labels from replays (pilot)
steps.note: 400 games: both leads found in 100% of sides; all four brought Pokémon seen in 81.5% (partial sides: use known subset).

steps.name: Time candidate network sizes
steps.note: Measured at batch 256 with other jobs running (so times are upper bounds): 1M params 4.8 min/epoch; 2.5M (dim 192, 4 layers) 7.3 min; 3.4M (192 x 6) 10 min; 4.2M (256 x 4) 10 min. Decision latency is about 5-6 ms for all (feature calculation dominates). Chosen: 192 x 4 layers, about 1.2 h for 10 epochs.

steps.name: Preview head and loss added to the policy; tests
steps.note: Preview head (bring four = sum of per-Pokémon scores over the 15 sets of four; leads = scored pairs), preview_labels.py builds the training data, preview.py has the loss and LearnedPreview for the agent hook. train_il --preview trains it alongside the battle policy. 54 tests pass, including full games with an untrained learned preview.

steps.name: Pilot imitation run (10% data), then full run; check both gates
steps.note: Full run done (192x4, 10 epochs, 13,900 games): 56.2% top-1 (older 128x3: 57.8%); overfits after epoch 3. Gates, rule-based preview: vs random 86.2% (not 90), known teams 49.3% (older model 50.0%, rule-based pilot 57.0%): level with the older model. Learned preview is much worse: 75.8% vs random and 38.0% on known teams, about 11 points below the rule-based preview. Keep the rule-based preview until the learned one beats it.

steps.name: Self-play league trainer (pilot, then full run)
steps.note: Pilot done (3 iterations; found and fixed a hang with few games and added anti-stalling guards: 30-turn cap, idle-turn penalty, protect/heal share tracked). Speed: about 85-95 s per 48 games, so 128 games x 30 iterations is about 2 hours. Reward = half win/loss + half health margin. Full run next. Full run started 2026-10-18: 30 iterations x 128 games, from il_policy_v3, log results/selfplay_run6.log.

gates.name: Good
gates.text: Wins at least 55% against the rule-based player (greedy-blind) on held-out teams of every kind, paired games (each side pilots both teams) so 50% is parity: +5 points. 1,200 games. Trick Room teams and the 10 known teams are reported as sub-scores.

gates.name: Sub-score: 10 known Trick Room teams
gates.text: Win rate piloting the 10 known-good Trick Room teams against held-out strong teams (rule-based pilot: 57.0%). Reported, not a gate.

rules: A 5-minute pilot on a tenth of the data before every full run
One change at a time; no input or output changes in the middle of a run
Up to about 2 hours per run
Archive each run's log and model under a run name and write the result into docs/learned-agent.md the same day
Results within about ±4 points are noise: report them as level
Tests pass before any full run
